name: Negative Concord
pattern: clause with verbal negation and/or multiple negative expressions interpreted together

entry.name: Negative Concord
entry.pattern: clause with verbal negation and/or multiple negative expressions interpreted together

1.definition: Expresses a single negation through more than one negative-marked item in the relevant variety.

projection.target: In concord varieties this can mean nobody was told. A two-negation interpretation is also possible in other systems or with a specially contrastive context.
projection.evidence: See the cited discussion and the constructed illustration.

curious.title: Two negative words, one negation
curious.summary: In some varieties of English, more than one negative word in a clause can express a single negation.
curious.body: In I didn't tell nobody about it, both didn't and nobody are negative words. In varieties with negative concord, the sentence expresses one negation and can mean that nobody was told. Other systems can read two negative words differently, as two negations. A specially contrastive context can also bring out that two-negation reading. The reading depends on the variety, not on the words alone.
curious.try: Listen for a sentence with two negative words, such as didn't and nobody. Does the speaker seem to mean one negation or two?

teacher.summary: Explains how multiple negative expressions can express a single negation, with the reading depending on the variety.
teacher.explain: Negative concord is a pattern in which a clause with verbal negation and/or multiple negative expressions is interpreted as expressing a single negation. In I didn't tell nobody about it, the interpretation in a concord variety is that nobody was told. A two-negation interpretation is also possible in other systems or with a specially contrastive context. Related patterns include primary-auxiliary negation and the determinative no.
teacher.terms: Negative concord is the term this dictionary uses for the single-negation interpretation.

contrasts.text: I didn't tell nobody about it.
contrasts.note: In a concord variety, one negation, meaning nobody was told.

watch_for: A learner might read two negative words as cancelling each other to give a positive meaning, when in a concord variety they express one negation.
A learner might assume that every variety interprets two negative words the same way.
teacher.activity: Discuss with students how the sentence I didn't tell nobody about it would be understood in a variety with negative concord and in a system with two negations. Ask them to explain the difference in meaning each reading gives.

checked.note: Fixed: cut the 'double negative / double negation' term from teacher terms (the entry does not support it as a label for the form); curious body trimmed a sentence claiming the dictionary describes each reading, which the entry does not do.
